title: Chapter 2720: The Beginning of the Invasion
content:
Chapter 2720: The Beginning of the Invasion

As Yuan entered the Level 4 Black Zone, an immense pressure descended upon him like an invisible mountain.

Every entity he sensed radiated a presence comparable to the boss of the 48th floor, some so powerful that he couldn’t even gauge their strength.

The humans of this world refused to explore the Level 4 Black Zone for a reason, and the last person to set foot there was Tian Yuchen, but that was over two thousand years ago.

Yet despite the overwhelming danger his surroundings posed, Yuan felt no dread. If anything, he was unusually calm.

However, Yuan moved carefully and stealthily, using Shadow Veil to completely mask his presence as he moved through the void.

’What exactly am I doing...?’ Yuan wondered as he ventured deeper into the Black Zone.

He had assumed the Void Hunter would eventually make an appearance, but several hours had already passed since he entered the Black Zone, and it was still nowhere to be seen.

Luckily, he hadn’t encountered any Void Specters so far, since he’d been deliberately avoiding them.

His gaze drifted toward the Grand Tree in the far distance, standing at the edge of the horizon. The longer he stared at it, the stronger his desire to approach grew, as though some instinct deep within him urged him forward.

’Since I’m already here, I might as well investigate it,’ Yuan thought as he shifted his attention toward the Grand Tree.

In his mind, only two outcomes were possible: either he would reach the Grand Tree first, or the Void Hunter would appear and stop him before he got there.

However, the closer Yuan got to the Grand Tree, the more he realized reaching it undetected by the Void Specters would be impossible, as their numbers increased drastically the deeper he ventured.

Suddenly, the world trembled, and a crack appeared in the sky, prompting Yuan to look up.

A second later, the crack began to repair itself, and within two more seconds, the sky returned to normal.

’What the hell are they even doing? Why attack only to stop and give the barrier time to recover?’ Yuan shook his head at the Eternals’ puzzling behavior.

He couldn’t understand why their attacks were so infrequent. If they had attacked relentlessly, the barrier would have likely shattered long ago.

’It’s almost as if they’re not really trying to invade—’

Yuan’s thoughts were abruptly interrupted when he sensed a sudden change in the atmosphere.

By the time he lowered his gaze from the sky, a familiar figure was already standing a few hundred meters in front of him.

"I was beginning to worry that you wouldn’t show up," Yuan said with a smile.

"..."

The Void Hunter remained silent.

Even so, Yuan immediately assumed a fighting stance, clearly preparing for battle.

"You..."

The Void Hunter suddenly spoke.

"You do not belong here..." the Void Hunter said, making Yuan raise an eyebrow.

"You do not qualify to be here..."

Before Yuan could even respond, the Void Hunter raised an arm and pointed a finger at him.

The next instant, Yuan’s entire world turned black, as though the void itself had swallowed him.

The darkness lasted only a brief moment, and when his vision returned, Yuan found himself far from where he had originally been.

Yuan looked around and quickly determined that he had been teleported back to the Level 3 Black Zone.

Of course, the Void Hunter had followed him.

"What do you want from me?" Yuan asked.

"Become worthy," the Void Hunter responded, greatly surprising Yuan.

Not only had it given him a proper response, but its speech also sounded different from before. Compared to their previous encounters, it was like listening to someone who had once barely known how to speak but had since become somewhat proficient.

"To become worthy, do I have to defeat you or something?" Yuan asked.

The Void Hunter quietly nodded.

"Then fight me properly. I know I can’t defeat you in my current state, but at the very least, I want to know just how vast the gap between us really is."

The Void Hunter remained silent. Although Yuan couldn’t see its expression, he could somehow feel that it was contemplating his request.

Suddenly, an overwhelming surge of energy erupted from the Void Hunter, its unfathomable presence instantly spreading across half the world.

"?!?!"

Yuan’s eyes widened with shock, and his complexion paled.

The Void Hunter’s aura was so immense that he couldn’t even tell the difference between them!

’That’s got to be on the level of a Prime Eternal!’ Yuan cried inwardly.

"How the hell am I supposed to defeat you?! You’re asking for the impossible!" Yuan exclaimed a moment later.

"That is for you to figure out..." the Void Hunter responded, then suddenly raised its head toward the sky.

Shortly afterward, the world was struck once again, and another crack appeared across the barrier.

This time, however, the damage was far more severe.

If one looked closely, they could even see a tiny hole pierced through the barrier.

Of course, the damage was quickly repaired—but not before several invaders slipped through.

Yuan watched, frowning deeply, as several black dots descended from the sky.

Four.

Yuan counted four of them, and shortly after entering Earth, they scattered in different directions.

’One of them is heading toward Gaia’s Heaven!’ Yuan cried inwardly upon realizing this.

Without hesitation, he turned his back on the Void Hunter and chased after the invader.

The Void Hunter made no attempt to pursue him and merely watched in silence.

Once Yuan disappeared from view, it vanished into thin air.

Meanwhile, the people of Gaia’s Heaven had also witnessed the invaders breach their world and immediately began preparing to confront them.

Sirens blared throughout the base, and as soon as the soldiers heard them, they dropped whatever they were doing and rushed to the Parade Deck, where Supreme General Tian was already waiting.

"The time has come! Gaia created the military for this exact moment! Although there are only four of them so far, do not underestimate them and do not show any mercy!"

The soldiers erupted into thunderous cheers, their fighting spirit surging through the air, mostly because the invaders’ numbers were far lower than any of them had anticipated.
